race_context: John Glenn School Corporation (JGSC) is headquartered in Walkerton and serves Walkerton and North Liberty in St. Joseph County plus territory in Marshall County; its schools are John Glenn High School, Urey Middle School, North Liberty Elementary and Walkerton Elementary {wiki_jgsc}. The state list ties each township seat to LaPorte, Marshall and St. Joseph counties {in_list}. Superintendent Christopher Winchell said in January 2026 that the district received a 'Max Levy Appeal' after annexing Greene Township {jg_jan6}.

Enrollment: state counts were 1,999 students in 2023-24, 1,993 in 2024-25 and 1,960 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. In September 2026 Winchell put enrollment at about 1,910, said it has declined by about 100 students since 2020, and said the district budgets around a 'sweet spot' of 1,950; about 20 students are in the district's virtual school {jg_sep1}.

The board has seven members: Jared Egger, Kathy Jaworski, Ryan Knowlton, Christian Mattix, Christine Carson, Todd McGaughey and Carissa Smith. In January 2026 the board, which rotates officers each year, chose Knowlton as president, Smith as vice president and Mattix as secretary, and kept member pay at $2,000 a year {jg_jan6}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: one each for Liberty, Lincoln and Polk townships, matching the state list {in_list}. All three are held by members first elected in 2022: Christine Carson (Liberty), Carissa Smith (Lincoln) and Todd McGaughey (Polk) {sbt_2022}. All three are running again; Carson and McGaughey are unopposed, and Smith faces Dennis Leon Metz, Jr. {in_list}.

Budget and SEA 1 (2026): Winchell told the board in January that the district's circuit breaker losses, tied to property taxes, rose from $290,000 in its 2025 budget order to $680,000, and that he expected them to grow in 2027 and 2028 {jg_jan6}. In April he said the district is working to cut $500,000 from its operations budget and that the property-tax cuts in SB 1 'will affect us directly'; the board voted 5-1 to buy Chromebooks partly to replace staff laptops, after a teacher said the change 'was not positively received at all' {jg_apr7}. In September he said St. Joseph County's certified assessed value for John Glenn came in lower than nearby areas' roughly 4% growth, as an earlier outside analysis had predicted {jg_sep1}.

Facilities bond (fall 2026): after putting Urey Middle School work on hold during the previous budget cycle because of SB 1 uncertainty, the board held public hearings Sept. 15 and Oct. 6, 2026 on renovating and improving facilities, buying buses, equipment and technology, and possibly buying real estate {jg_aug4}{jg_hearings}. On Oct. 6 it made a preliminary determination to issue up to $14,945,000 in bonds over up to 20 years (23 if leases) {jg_prelim}. The district's notice estimates the debt service tax rate would rise from $0.3997 to $0.4243 in 2027 and then fall to $0.3807, for a projected net increase of $0.00 over the current rate as older debt matures {jg_prelim}. Winchell said Urey's HVAC, windows, doors, carpet, lighting and paint would be the focus, along with some high school needs and elementary playground equipment {jg_sep1}.

Other issues: in summer 2026 the board chose the least restrictive option under the new state cell phone law, allowing phones on campus as long as they stay in lockers or backpacks {jg_jun16}. The 2026-27 school year began with three days canceled because of a storm, and the district planned to seek a state waiver for them {jg_sep1}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign website for these races. Minutes of the January through September 2026 board meetings reviewed for this guide record no public comment at any of them {jg_jan6}{jg_sep1}.
